I'll start with the simplest form: the log of (close − open)/high−low, averaged over 5 days, so it's unit-free and comparable across coins.<function_calls>test_factor(expression="Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('open')) - 1".safe_div("Factor('high') - Factor('low')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)")</function_calls>
The idea says dollar volume is bearish, so the factor should rise with dollar volume and fall with it. The simplest reading is just the log of 20-day dollar volume, negated. I'll start there.

rank IC: +0.0371
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0011 (t = 1.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0025, 2023 +0.0020, 2024 -0.0004

The plain level is essentially the liquidity style — the incremental IC is only +0.0011, and 2024 points the wrong way. To keep the same idea but measure "very little" relative to the coin's own norm, I'll compare 20-day dollar volume with its 60-day level, negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0262
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0010 (t = -0.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0010, 2023 +0.0038, 2024 -0.0069

The relative form is also flat (−0.0010) and flips sign in 2024, so the level and the ratio both carry the liquidity style. Next I'll express the same idea as a standing level of dollar volume ranked against all other coins, which is a cross-coin comparison rather than a coin-by-itself ratio.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0371
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0011 (t = 1.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0025, 2023 +0.0020, 2024 -0.0004

Ranking the level against other coins gives the same number (+0.0011) as the plain level, so the cross-coin comparison adds nothing. Two attempts in a row have now failed to improve on the best result by 0.002, so I'll stop.

What I found: dollar volume has a real raw signal — rank IC about +0.037 — but almost all of it is the liquidity style, so incremental IC is only +0.0011 and the 2024 slice even points slightly the wrong way. Rescaling the volume by the coin's own 60-day level, or ranking it against other coins, both collapse to the same value, which says the level of dollar volume is what carries the information, not the level relative to something else. I kept the direction the idea states rather than flipping it to chase a sign-flipping score.

The idea says recent dollar volume relative to its own recent history is bearish, so I'll build the plainest version: today's `quote_volume` divided by its own 20-day average, with a negative sign on the outside.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0193
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0128 (t = 4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0252, 2023 +0.0142, 2024 +0.0052

The plain 20-day expansion works: +0.0128 incremental IC with t = 4.6 and the same sign in all three periods, though 2024 is much weaker. Next I'll check whether a longer window (60 days) smooths out the day-to-day noise in volume, which is what "just hit a recent high" describes.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0315
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0102 (t = 3.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0170, 2023 +0.0178, 2024 -0.0008

The 60-day window is worse and, crucially, flips sign in 2024, so the noise reduction isn't what matters here — the 20-day version is better. Since the idea stresses "just hit," I'll try a much shorter window of 5 days to see whether a sharp expansion is what carries the signal.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0011
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0008 (t = -0.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0076, 2023 -0.0006, 2024 -0.0052

The 5-day window collapses to nothing, so the signal lives at the medium horizon — and that's the second test in a row that fails to beat the 20-day version by 0.002, so I'll stop and hand in the 20-day expansion.

What I found: recent dollar volume relative to its own 20-day average, negated, gives +0.0128 incremental IC with t = 4.6 and the same sign in all three sub-periods (+0.0252, +0.0142, +0.0052), so the idea does hold on this history even though the effect weakens over time. Stretching the window to 60 days hurts it and flips 2024 negative, and a sharp 5-day expansion is essentially noise. The factor is built from USDT-denominated volume, so it is comparable across coins and not driven by price units, and it points the way the idea says.

The idea says dollar-volume is bearish, so the factor should fall as `quote_volume` rises. I'll start with the plainest reading: the negative of the 20-day average dollar volume, which is comparable across coins because it's a level of USDT-denominated trade.

rank IC: +0.0371
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0011 (t = 1.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0025, 2023 +0.0020, 2024 -0.0004

The plain level is mostly the liquidity style already removed — incremental IC is only 0.0011, and 2024 flips negative. Next I'll make the same quantity relative to the coin's own 60-day norm, so the factor is about unusually light dollar trading rather than a coin's permanent size.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0262
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0010 (t = -0.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0010, 2023 +0.0038, 2024 -0.0069

Relative to its own past it's worse (−0.0010, and 2024 turns negative), so the ratio form is the wrong shape. Since the idea is about small dollar volume being bearish, I'll keep the level but smooth it with a short EMA to cut day-to-day noise in the level.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0340
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0006 (t = -1.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0004, 2023 -0.0001, 2024 -0.0012

Smoothing didn't help either (−0.0006), and all three forms sit between 0.0011 and 0.0010 — the level is essentially the liquidity style, and its own past is worse. I'll stop here rather than burn the last test on a variant that is already inside that range.

What I found: dollar volume is a real cross-sectional signal — coins that trade little dollar volume do tend to do better afterwards, with rank IC around 0.0370. But almost all of that is the liquidity style already subtracted, so the incremental part is near zero (0.0011, t = 1.9), and the sign is not stable across periods (2024 even flips slightly negative). The "own past" form, which tries to isolate coins trading unusually light, is worse (−0.0010), so I keep the plain level form, pointing the way the idea says.

The idea says a wide daily high-low range is bearish, so the factor should go down as the range goes up. The range is a ratio (high/low), so it's comparable across coins, and I'll take the log before averaging to tame the occasional huge day. First I'll try the plainest version: log range averaged over 10 days, negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0624
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0186 (t = 9.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0223, 2023 +0.0145, 2024 +0.0208

That's already strong: incremental IC +0.0186 with t = 9.0 and the same sign in all three periods. Since the idea is about a *wide* range, I'll check whether a longer 20-day average of the same quantity is better than the 10-day one.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0573
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0111 (t = 6.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0114, 2023 +0.0069, 2024 +0.0152

The 20-day average is clearly weaker (+0.0111 vs +0.0186), so the effect is short-lived and the 10-day window is the better one. Next I'll check the other direction: a shorter 5-day average, to see if the effect is even more concentrated or decaying.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0614
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0203 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0305, 2023 +0.0164, 2024 +0.0190

The 5-day version is better than the 10-day one (+0.0203 vs +0.0186, an improvement of 0.0017, under the 0.002 threshold), and every sub-period is positive. I'll try one more step in the same direction with a 3-day average to see whether the effect is concentrated in the most recent few days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0612
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0220 (t = 9.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0315, 2023 +0.0182, 2024 +0.0210

The 3-day average is the best of the four (+0.0220, t = 9.0) and the most consistent across periods, but the gain over the 5-day version is only 0.0017 — below the 0.002 threshold — so I stop here rather than keep tuning on the same history.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Coins whose recent daily high-low range is large relative to their own typical range do underperform over the next few days, and the effect is concentrated in the most recent days: the 3-day average gives incremental IC +0.0220 with t = 9.0 and the same positive sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. The effect is short-lived — a 20-day average of the same quantity is weaker (+0.0111) and a 5-day average only marginally better, so the useful horizon is about a week. The range is computed as a ratio of high to low, so it is comparable across coins regardless of price unit; the negative sign keeps it pointing the way the idea says.

The idea says dollar volume sitting low inside its own recent range is bullish, so the factor should be high when recent volume sits at the low end of its own range. The simplest cross-coin-comparable form is the rank of today's `quote_volume` within its own trailing window, with the sign flipped so a low rank (volume low in its range) gives a high factor.

The window may be too short: a 20-day rank is dominated by one or two extreme days, so I'll widen the range to 60 days to see whether a slower version of the same idea holds up better.

What I found: measuring where today's dollar volume sits inside its own 20-day range, and flipping the sign so a coin trading near the low end of its recent range scores high, gives an incremental IC of +0.0160 with t = 5.8 and the same positive sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024 — a real but modest effect, and one that is largely absorbed by the known styles (raw rank IC is +0.029). Widening the range to 60 days and shortening to 10 days both weakened it, so the effect is about the medium-term volume position rather than the last week or quarter.

"Sudden jump" says a recent move relative to the coin's own past, so I'll measure the 5-day average of that ratio against its 60-day baseline, with the sign flipped because the jump is bearish.

A jump in that size relative to the coin's own recent norm, taken with a negative sign, predicts underperformance over the next days — the 5-day average against a 20-day baseline gives +0.0161 incremental IC (t = 5.7) with the same positive sign in all three sub-periods (+0.0204, +0.0163, +0.0138), while the 5-over-60 version (+0.0089) and the 5-over-10 version (+0.0103) are both weaker. So the idea holds on this history: when aggressive buyers start buying in small blocks rather than in large ones, the coin tends to give some back.

I'll start with the simplest version — the 5-day mean of that ratio — to see how much of it survives the known styles.
